title: Complementary 3D color codes for transversal quantum logic
authors: Friederike Butt, Luis Colmenarez, Erik Weilandt, Tom Peham, Robert Wille, Markus Müller
abstract: Transversal logical gates provide a direct route to fault-tolerant quantum computation, but the Eastin-Knill theorem forbids a universal transversal gate set within a single quantum error-correcting code. We propose a hybrid architecture based on the tetrahedral three-dimensional color code and its Hadamard-transformed counterpart, which we call the H-tetrahedral code. The two encodings support complementary transversal non-Clifford operations. Combined with bitwise Hadamard transformations that switch between the two encodings and a one-way transversal logical CNOT from the tetrahedral code to the H-tetrahedral code, these operations realize an almost-universal transversal logical gate set that enables both the creation of entanglement and logical states with magic. We complete a universal gate set through a pieceably fault-tolerant round-robin construction of a logical controlled-$Z$ gate between two H-tetrahedral codes. This logical entangling gate is interleaved with reduced-overhead Steane-type syndrome extraction using logical two-dimensional color-code auxiliary qubits. Our construction provides a new route toward implementing classically hard-to-simulate quantum algorithms where magic and most entangling operations are transversal while the resource overhead is concentrated in a small number of non-transversal Clifford entangling operations.
summary: The paper addresses the challenge of implementing a universal set of gates fault-tolerantly by proposing a hybrid architecture combining two related 3D color codes. This combination allows for most necessary operations (like magic state injection and entanglement) to remain transversal, significantly reducing resource overhead compared to fully non-transversal methods.
main_problem: Achieving fault-tolerant quantum computation requires implementing a universal set of logical gates transversally, which is forbidden by the Eastin–Knill theorem on a single Quantum Error-Correcting (QEC) code.
main_result: The authors propose a hybrid architecture using two complementary color codes (tetrahedral and H-tetrahedral) to realize an almost-universal transversal gate set, completing universality via a fault-tolerant round-robin construction for the logical controlled-Z gate.
method: The approach combines operations across two related QEC codes, utilizing one-way transversal gates and decomposing complex entangling gates into sequences of simpler, fault-tolerant components.
model_or_system: The system is based on a hybrid architecture combining the tetrahedral three-dimensional color code and its Hadamard-transformed counterpart ($	ext{H-tetrahedral}$ code), specifically analyzed using the $[[15, 1, 3]]$ encoding.
key_observables: Logical state fidelities ($F_{CZ}|0+angle$, $F_{CZ}|1+angle$), transversal gate support (CNOT, Toffoli), and resource overheads for non-transversal operations.
important_parameters: The code distance parameters are analyzed, including the relationship between effective X-error distance ($d_X$) and Z-error distance ($d_Z = 3d^2 + 1/4$).
main_assumptions: The initial transversal CNOT gate only works in one direction (tetrahedral control $	o$ H-tetrahedral target), necessitating the round-robin construction for full universality.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate stabilizer support on both codes, detail the one-way transversal CNOT operation, show the possibility of a Toffoli gate, and depict fault-tolerant syndrome extraction steps using auxiliary qubits.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the need for hybrid codes due to the Eastin-Knill theorem; it details the construction of an almost-universal set via complementary transversal operations (CNOT); finally, it completes universality by constructing a fault-tolerant logical controlled-Z gate using pieceable round-robin techniques.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete, resource-aware protocols for achieving universal quantum computation by cleverly circumventing theoretical limitations using structured code combinations, which is highly relevant to physical implementations on various hardware platforms.

Figure 2. Transversal operations in the hybrid architecture. (a) If the control qubit is encoded in the [[15, 1, 3]] code and the target in the Hadamard-transformed [[15, 1, 3]]H code, cell-like stabilizers propagate to face-like stabilizers. This operation preserves the codespace because both control and target are a +1-eigenstate of the X-cells. The transversal CNOT gate in the reverse direction (b) does not preserve the codespace, because an X-face propagates from control to the target code that is not an eigenstate of the respective face-like stabilizer.
